name: Settings list
summary: A schema-driven group of settings rows — label left, control right — reusing existing DS controls.
lead: TWO custom elements — <aha-settings-list> (a spacing-only, schema-driven group surface) and <aha-settings-item> (a labelled row with a `control` slot). Pass a settings schema (`.schema` = { sections:[{ label, description?, rows:[{ key, label, description?, control:{ type, …props } }] }] }) and it RENDERS the rows, instantiating each control from an existing DS element (aha-switch / aha-checkbox / aha-input …) — reuse, never a re-implemented control — and emits a `change` event { key, value, name }. The by-hand slot form is still supported. Spacing-only hierarchy: no divider lines, no card/box around plain settings. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens. Zero drift.
codeNote: Same elements, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes them via thin attribute wrappers; Vue binds the custom elements natively. Defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

props.name: schema
props.desc: (list, property) Settings schema { sections:[{ label, description?, rows:[{ key, label, description?, control }] }] } — an array is treated as one section's rows; renders rows and reuses DS controls. Also settable as a JSON `schema` attribute for the build-free HTML form

props.name: label
props.desc: Group header (a 1–3 word noun phrase); on <aha-settings-item> it is the setting name. Ignored when a schema supplies section labels

props.name: description
props.desc: (item) An optional must-see consequence line under the label — default none

props.name: control
props.desc: (item) The DS control on the right — <aha-switch>, <aha-checkbox>, <aha-input>… slotted by hand, or named in a schema row's `control:{ type }` and instantiated for you

events.name: change
events.desc: (schema form) Fired when any rendered control changes — value is the control's boolean/string state, key is the row's key

whenToUse.when: a group of related on/off or choice settings in a panel, page or drawer
values are submitted together with validation and a submit step
one setting that applies on its own

opinion.note: Name each setting as a noun phrase (no leading verb — the control says on/off). Use a toggle for immediate effect, a checkbox for consent/saved-together — never mix in one group. Hierarchy is spacing, never lines or boxes; keep help text to at most one line per group. See the settings pattern for grouping, sub-settings and the danger zone.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — this is the reusable component form of the settings pattern (parts/settings.guide.md): label/control rows, spacing-only grouping, no dividers or boxes. It composes existing DS controls via a slot. A deliberate, documented AhaSlides surface.
